scope: Separate offline FP32 batched CPU supplied-paragraph reader profile, not the FP16 profile or a hosted/API latency claim

prior_profile: R9 stopped with zero final questions. Its timings and diagnostics remain immutable. The same unused 200-question final pool is reused; ten new pilot paragraphs are disjoint from every prior planned or attempted question context.
method: The existing system prompt, Unicode JSON serialization, quote validation and draft policy are retained. Batched greedy generation is new evaluation-only code. Scoped complete-document language metadata follows the real store schema. EOS padding is excluded from per-sequence token counts. Native batch calls and logical sequence completions are distinct.
cohort_rule: Use timing only before inspecting answers, correctness or routing. Require at least eight completed native generations. Conservative per-question cost is 1.25 times the worst attempted batch time divided by its requested sequence count, including failed/interrupted batches. Reserve twice total setup and 20 percent of the remaining 18000 seconds. Select a balanced prefix in complete batches, at most 200 questions. Below forty, stop without a final run.
failure_policy: No retry of failed generations. Retain all requested slots. Batch-wide failures remain batch-wide unknown outcomes; never assign a single bad sequence to every row without that qualification. Raw successful generations are checkpointed before assembly. Interrupted native token counts remain unknown.
metrics: The same strict candidate short-answer EM/F1 and public-reference abstention rules as R9. Report requested and completed-only denominators, answerability strata, invalid metric fields, format/runtime failures, output-cap reaches, unknown/interrupted rows and draft/hold states. Always-abstain is the same-cohort control.
uncertainty: 2000 seed-19 nominal question bootstrap, paired differences from always abstain, and whole-article cluster sensitivity with a minimum ten article clusters. These selected public dev questions may occur in model training and are not new human gold.
interpretation: Precision, batching and thread count differ from R9. No causal claim of better answer quality relative to FP16 is licensed. No default model or release policy changes are licensed by this research run.
publication: Only numeric records, hashes, identities and bounded aggregates. Source text, reference spans and raw model outputs remain private. Earlier reports remain unchanged.
